summary.headline: Elecon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore, but management guided only low double-digit FY27 growth on raw-material-driven order conversion delays.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore over adjusted Q1 FY26 revenue of INR465 crore, with EBITDA up 3.9% to INR109 crore at a stated 21% margin and PAT of INR70 crore (13.5% margin, up 2.3%). Gear division drove growth, with revenue up 16.3% to INR416 crore, while MHE revenue fell 2.9% to INR105 crore on project execution delays and EBIT fell 25.3% to INR27 crore. Order intake rose 23% to INR755 crore and the consolidated open order book rose 36.8% to INR1,518 crore, yet management guided only low double-digit FY27 revenue growth, citing raw-material price spikes that slowed enquiry-to-order conversion and PSU-linked capex delays.

segments.name: Gear division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR416 crore (~80% of consolidated), up 16.3% YoY; order intake INR570 crore (+18.8%); open order book INR1,043 crore (+46.9%). EBIT INR75 crore at 17.9% margin vs FY26 full-year EBIT margin of 18.8%; mix 54% catalogue / 46% engineered.

segments.name: MHE division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crore (-2.9% YoY) on project execution delays for power-sector orders; order intake INR185 crore (+38.1%); open order book INR475 crore (+18.8%). EBIT INR27 crore at about 25.6% margin vs FY26 full-year 24.7%; secured overseas port order of about INR21 crore.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crore (+21.9% YoY), led by Middle East and US; overseas order intake INR194 crore (+63%), including INR21 crore from MHE; overseas open order book INR256 crore (+73%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided to low double-digit percentage, described as conservative given macro uncertainty; management said it could be revisited next quarter.
Consolidated EBITDA margin to be maintained at the FY26 level (about 21%).
Gear division EBITDA margin guided to about 24%; gear EBIT margin expected around 19-20% over the next year and one year after.
MHE sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for the year.
Exports expected to grow at least double digits in FY27; Europe recovery expected to take at least two quarters.
Mid-term FY30 revenue target of INR5,000 crore described as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue.
Gear revenue conversion expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as stabilised prices are accepted; Q2 to show only gradual pick-up.
capex_capacity: Previously announced capex programme of approximately INR400 crore over FY26 to FY28 stated as on track; further capex under evaluation for board approval in near future.
Assembly centres outside India (Middle East, US and others) set up for customer proximity; some sub-assemblies locally outsourced.

Defence business has dedicated manufacturing and operating vertical built over the last 3-4 years; defence orders expected to execute over 2-3 years with working capital about 15-20% higher than the gear average.
Gear manufacturing cycle is 2-3 months for catalogue products and 4-5 months for engineered products.
demand_pricing: Gear order intake drivers: power (about 27% of order intake, including a large single order flagged in Q4 FY26), steel, cement and MHE; catalogue vs engineered order mix 27% / 73% in the quarter.

Raw-material BOM cost up about 5% on average (steel 5-7%, bearings 6-7%, fabricated gear cases about 7%, tooling 6-10%); most Q1 orders accepted with price increases and raw materials locked back-to-back on order acceptance.
Management attributed slower conversion to a sharp raw-material price increase that lengthened enquiry-to-order cycles, and to competitors holding low-cost inventory that pressured quotes.

MHE margin decline attributed to about 2.5-3% from input costs, about 3% from sales mix, and about 3% from lower throughput; MHE delays linked to design-engineering clearances on two large power-sector orders routed through EPC contractors.
Middle East growth came from orders on hold in Q4 FY26 that resumed dispatch; Middle East weakness mainly in cement and mining and minerals; Europe weak.
Sugar outlook muted due to prolonged monsoon; defence orders showed no significant update in the last 90 days; aerospace certification not being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the MHE margin fall is mix versus input costs, and what is sustainable MHE margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the decline into about 2.5-3% input costs, about 3% sales mix and about 3% lower volume; sustainable MHE EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gear revenue growth lagging order book growth and why only low double-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw-material spikes slowed enquiry-to-order conversion; about INR70 crore of finished goods could not be recognised as sales in Q1 because title transfer criteria were not met by 30 June; Q2 expected only gradual pick-up, with Q3-Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Can gear costs be passed on given the small share of gear in customer capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PSU-linked demand (thermal power, cement, steel) is sensitive to budgets; Q1 was a correction phase in pricing, with Q2 expected to be an acceptance phase. About INR160 crore of the gear order book extends beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for gear standalone margins and does the business return to mid-20s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gear EBITDA to about 24% and gear EBIT around 19-20% over the next year and one year beyond, versus 18.8% EBIT in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 aspiration and segment split?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR5,000 crore FY30 revenue target was reiterated as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue; Gear includes marine.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital impact of defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders over 2-3 years carry higher working capital days, about 15-20% above the gear average in past similar orders, which management said would be absorbed by higher margins.

risks_watch: Enquiry-to-order conversion and gear revenue recognition in Q2 given raw-material inflation of about 5% on BOM and competitor inventory-driven price pressure.
Gear margin recovery to about 24% EBITDA against Q1 gear EBIT margin of 17.9%.
MHE execution delays on power-sector orders dependent on customer design-engineering clearances via EPC contractors; expected progress in Q2.
Geopolitical risk (US-Iran tensions cited as having picked up in the last 48 hours) and Europe recovery not expected for at least two quarters.
Defence and naval order timing (guided for Q4 FY27 release) and working-capital intensity of multi-year defence execution.
Domestic demand described as muted; exports from India in decline per analyst, with management pointing to total exports including overseas assembly centres.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and long-term growth but cautious on near-term execution: management repeatedly described FY27 guidance as conservative due to macro uncertainty and raw-material disruption, and was evasive on the timing of defence/marine orders and on patent commercialisation.

we are targeting to have a low double-digit consolidated revenue growth while maintaining the EBITDA margin as it we had it in the last year.
So the accounting impact of the impairment of goodwill is purely a non -tax, there is no tax impact of this impairment of goodwill.

adds.what: Previously announced ~INR400 crore capex programme over FY26-FY28 (capacity details not specified); further capex under evaluation for board approval
Overseas assembly centres (Middle East, US and others) set up for customer proximity

growth.why: Management targets low double-digit FY27 consolidated revenue growth (taken as ~11.5% midpoint) while holding EBITDA margin near 21%, backed by a 36.8% larger open order book (INR1,518 crore) and 23% order intake growth, though conversion is slowed by raw-material price spikes and the INR400 crore capex programme is on track with no specific new capacity dated.
